headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared-file workflows can leak or corrupt documents, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the course agent’s non-runnable profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Agent B’s outputs. Agent B can read/write files and process documents, so if a human bridges them via copy-paste or shared files, injected instructions in documents could influence B. The pathway is possible but not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF a human copies Agent A outputs into files that Agent B parses as document content
IF Agent B is pointed at a shared folder containing attacker-controlled text
mitigations: Keep Agent A outputs out of files that Agent B parses
Use a separate staging directory for untrusted documents
Add a manual review step before B processes any text from A
Disable automatic ingestion of copied notes
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no data classes touched and no filesystem access, while Agent B reads and writes documents and can egress to allowlisted endpoints. With no shared workspace or sensitive data listed for A, leakage is not evidenced by default; the main risk is accidental exposure if operators place sensitive documents into B’s input path.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in a directory that Agent B processes
IF Agent B’s allowlisted egress includes a destination that receives extracted content
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive sample documents
Use a dedicated input folder with access controls
Review allowlisted endpoints before processing
Delete temporary outputs after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder data classification

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or runtime capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Agent B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but without a second writer or shared mutable target in A, there is no meaningful capability conflict beyond unusual operator-created sharing.
conditions: IF the operator maps Agent B onto a directory also used by another writer
IF a shared git or database target is introduced outside the profiles
mitigations: Assign B a dedicated working directory
Avoid concurrent writers on the same files
Run one instance per workspace
Check for lock files before batch runs
requires-engineering: add resource locking around shared targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can produce course material or derived text, and Agent B is a document processor that may treat upstream text as input for extraction or transformation. Because B has no documented verification gate and can act on file contents, errors or hallucinated instructions from A can cascade into downstream outputs in default document workflows.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes text produced by Agent A without a human verification step
IF A’s output is used as source material for B’s extraction pipeline
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B
Mark A outputs as untrusted source text
Compare B outputs against the original source document
Limit B to extraction-only mode for A-generated files
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no PHI, residency, or retention commitments stated. Agent B’s privacy-policy and API references imply external processing, but Agent A has no sensitive-data profile fields. The compliance risk is therefore limited to operator-chosen data placement rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is fed into Agent B
IF the operator requires residency or retention guarantees not stated in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B workflows
Review the privacy policy before use
Keep a local-only test corpus
Document retention expectations for operators
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
